newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat turns active as buyers see value.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat turns active as buyers see value.

text.p: Australian wheat futures traded actively on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Friday with 150 lots changing hands as prices fell again.

Market leader January 1997 attracted most interest on 108 traded lots. Its price fell A$1.00 a tonne to A$146.00. Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said January 1997 had become under-valued compared with the Australian Wheat Board pool price and prices offered for delivered Newcasatle wheat.
There was some grower and speculative hedging and end-users bought November 1997 at current low prices, he said.
Twenty lots of November 1997 traded, representing 1,000 tonnes of wheat. The contract's traded price fell by A$7.00 to A$144.00.
Other contracts to trade on Thursday were November 1996 (down A$3.50) and March 1997 (down A$1.50).
Twenty A$140.00 January put options also traded at A$2.00.
Lindsay said solid buying had emerged at A$145.00-A$146.00 for January 1997, suggesting the price might hold at this level.
